A study in one call (simple layer)

Source: R/simple_v2.R
omop_study.Rd

omop_study() returns an ordinary omop_recipe: one indexed population (id name) and the requested outputs over it. It is exactly the advanced recipe below (recipe_to_code() prints it; print() lists every default the study chose):

  • population: omop_population(name, index = omop_index(index, select = select), filters = <require>, coverage = coverage); when index is an omop_population (e.g. from omop_new_users) or an omop_index, its index and criteria are kept and the requirements are ANDed after them.

  • require: prior_observation = n is omop_observed(before = n), followup = n is omop_observed(after = n), age = c(min, max) is omop_age_is(min, max) (NA = open), sex = "F" / "M" is omop_person(omop_where(gender_concept_id == 8532)) (8507), has = list(<events>) is omop_has(e, window = omop_window(NULL, 0)) (any time up to the index date), no_history_of = list(<events>) is omop_has_not(e, window = omop_window(NULL, -1)) (any time before the index date), in_cohort = id is omop_in_cohort(id); criterion objects are used as they are; all in the order given.

  • "baseline": a wide output with episode grain and every baseline variable (nested lists such as omop_history() are spliced in).

  • "survival": a survival output (competing_risk with two or more outcomes) with tar = omop_window(start, end) and the censor list of follow_up.

  • "long": a long output with the outcome events as sources (relative dates).

  • "panel": a dense person_period output with 30-day bins over the follow-up window, counting the outcomes.

The simple layer never exposes grain, ties or date handling: every output has episode grain, survival ties use the priority rule and dates are relative to the index; recipe_explain() states them. A "survival", "long" or "panel" output without outcomes, or a "baseline" output without baseline variables, is a structural error.

Usage

omop_study(
  index,
  select = c("first", "first_eligible", "all", "last"),
  require = list(),
  baseline = list(),
  outcomes = list(),
  follow_up = list(start = 1L, end = NULL, censor = c("observation_end", "death")),
  outputs = c("baseline", "survival"),
  name = "study",
  coverage = omop_coverage()
)

Arguments

index

An omop_event, omop_era, list(cohort_definition_id = ), omop_any_of(), an omop_index() or an indexed omop_population.

select

Index selection: "first" (default), "first_eligible", "all" or "last".

require

Named list of requirements (see Details).

baseline

Named list of baseline variables.

outcomes

Named list of outcome events.

follow_up

list(start = 1, end = NULL, censor = c("observation_end", "death")); give only the entries to change.

outputs

Subset of "baseline", "survival", "long", "panel".

name

Population name.

coverage

Observation coverage of the population (omop_coverage).

Value

An omop_recipe.

See also

omop_new_users, omop_ever, omop_recipe, recipe_to_code

Examples

t2dm <- omop_concept_set(201826, descendants = TRUE, name = "t2dm")
metf <- omop_concept_set(1503297, descendants = TRUE, name = "metformin")
mi <- omop_concept_set(4329847, descendants = TRUE, name = "mi")
study <- omop_study(
  index    = omop_new_users(metf, washout_days = 365),
  require  = list(prior_observation = 365,
                  has = list(omop_event("condition_occurrence", t2dm))),
  baseline = list(age = omop_age(), sex = omop_sex(),
                  hba1c = omop_value_at_index("measurement", 3004410, unit = 8554),
                  inpatient = omop_count("visit_occurrence", 9201, before = 365),
                  charlson = omop_score("charlson")),
  outcomes = list(mi = omop_event("condition_occurrence", mi)),
  follow_up = list(start = 1, end = NULL, censor = c("observation_end", "death")))
print(study)
